newsitem.title: USA: United has little cargo capacity for BA customers.
newsitem.headline: United has little cargo capacity for BA customers.

text.p: With most of its UK flights carrying nearly full cargo loads, United Airlines has little capacity to put at the disposal of British Airways customers affected by the BA cabin attendants strike, a United official said.

Carl Norris, director of cargo planning, told Reuters there are no plans to put on more flights or larger aircraft and no plans to operate any of United's Pacific freighters into London to pick up passenger or cargo business displaced by the strike.
"We have a limited ability to help" BA customers, Norris said.
While July is low season for cargo, cargo loads have remained solid after tailing off immediately after the July 4 holiday weekend in the U.S.

United's service parallels British Airways on several U.S.-UK routes that BA hopes to operate during the strike, including New York, Chicago and Los Angeles to London. United also flies Washington-London, a route BA has tentatively cancelled.
